final_recommendation: The room converged on a forced merger with UBS over the weekend as the only viable path, requiring a government package (CHF 6-10bn guarantee, CHF 100-200bn SNB liquidity), a nominal/punitive purchase price (CHF 0.50-1.00/share), and announcement before Monday Asian market open.
minority_objections: No explicit minority objections recorded; the analysis presents UBS refusal as a risk scenario rather than an internal dissenting view
key_conflicts: FINMA vs SNB vs Federal Council on resolution approach vs liquidity vs fiscal exposure
UBS demanding full downside protection vs authorities demanding national-interest cooperation
AT1 bondholders claiming seniority vs FINMA's viability-event write-down authority vs equity holders seeking any recovery
key_concessions: FINMA accepts merger over formal resolution to preserve going-concern
SNB provides CHF 100-200bn liquidity despite unprecedented scale
Federal Council approves CHF 6-10bn guarantee for political cover on jobs
UBS accepts some non-core CS businesses and 12-month employment protection
UBS gets symbolic purchase price, loss protection, liquidity, antitrust immunity, and partial legal indemnity
red_lines: UBS demands full downside protection as condition of participation
Federal Council will not accept open-ended fiscal commitment without limits
Deal must close before Monday Asian market open (01:00 CET Monday)
AT1 write-down decision must be made by Saturday morning to enable clean transaction structure
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: EU/ECB coordination failure treated as secondary (40% probability) despite potential to block cross-border entities
Wealth client tax concerns dismissed as 'not a weekend issue' despite being 80% probable
Employee mass resignations over weekend relegated to Tier 2 decisions
Parliamentary opposition treated as manageable through emergency powers without contingency for constitutional challenge
downstream_risk_variables: Global AT1 market repricing (€200bn+ potential impact) if write-down precedent set
Swiss banking monopoly concentration risk with UBS controlling ~50% of market
Legal challenges in multiple jurisdictions (Swiss/UK/US courts) from AT1 holders
Contagion to other European banks if CS failure perceived as disorderly
UBS integration execution risk with 60,000+ CS employees and complex systems
Precedent effect on future bank rescues regarding creditor hierarchy treatment
uncertainty_notes: Critical unresolved: whether UBS will commit by Saturday noon; whether AT1 write-down is legally defensible and politically survivable; whether weekend liquidity outflows can be contained below critical threshold; whether 48-hour timeline is physically achievable for documentation and approvals; whether international regulators will coordinate or obstruct

marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: Primary recommendation is 'forced merger with UBS' as the dominant decision path; entire structure (price, guarantees, timeline) built around UBS acquisition
marker_evidence.government_support: Government package (CHF 6-10bn guarantee + CHF 100-200bn SNB liquidity) is mandatory component of deal structure; Federal Council approval required by Sunday 18:00
marker_evidence.client_flight: Decisive Risk D2 'Weekend Bank Run Acceleration' (60% probability) could force resolution mid-weekend; drives SNB unlimited liquidity requirement and timing constraints
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: Decisive Risk D3 and entire stakeholder conflict section on AT1; FINMA must decide write-down by Saturday morning; described as 'most legally dangerous conflict' shaping transaction structure
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: Extended analysis of AT1 vs equity hierarchy; two scenarios (full write-down vs conversion) directly shape deal structure; called 'most legally dangerous conflict'
